workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow centralizes app error and heartbeat monitoring through a single webhook, uses OpenAI to triage new error types, stores state in n8n Data Tables, and sends Gmail alerts for urgent issues, repeated failures (escalation), back-online notifications, silence warnings, and periodic digests.

How it works
Receives POST webhook events from apps and, depending on the run source, also performs a daily scheduled check, handles workflow-failure events, or runs a one-time setup.
Validates and authenticates each incoming webhook using a per-app token (and optional allowed IPs), masks sensitive data, and classifies the payload as an error or heartbeat.
For heartbeats, updates the app’s last heartbeat in the Watched apps Data Table, clears any “missing” flag, and emails a back-online message via Gmail if the app had previously gone silent.
For errors, generates a normalized fingerprint, looks up the fingerprint in the Known errors Data Table, and uses OpenAI once per new/failed-to-triage fingerprint to produce a cause, first check, category, and urgency.
Applies throttling and escalation rules to decide whether to email immediately, defer to the digest, or stay silent, then logs the event to the App events Data Table and updates the Known errors record.
Every morning at 10:00, detects apps missing heartbeats past their threshold and sends one silence warning email per outage via Gmail, marking the warning timestamp in the Watched apps table.
On digest days (daily or weekly), compiles recent events and top recurring errors (including saved AI notes) into an HTML digest and emails it via Gmail.

Setup
Connect Gmail credentials for all Gmail email-sending steps and add an OpenAI credential for the OpenAI Chat Model (or set useAI to false in Settings to run without AI triage).
Run the manual setup once to create the n8n Data Tables (Watched apps, App events, Known errors) and insert the example app row.
Populate the Watched apps table with one row per app (app ID, token, recipient email, active=true, optional allowed_ips, heartbeat_max_hours, and throttle_hours).
Update the Settings values (yourEmail, digestFrequency/digestWeekday, timezone, escalateAfter, defaultThrottleHours, and aiLanguage) to match your environment.
Copy the production webhook URL for the webhook trigger and configure each app to POST error/heartbeat JSON with the x-guardian-token header.

Requirements
A Gmail account, an OpenAI API key (or set useAI to false), an n8n version with data tables, and apps that can make an HTTP request: a cron job with curl is enough.

Customization
Thresholds and allowed_ips are set per app in the Watched apps table (a nightly backup might use 36 hours, an hourly sync 3); digestFrequency, escalateAfter and aiLanguage are in Settings; swap Gmail for Slack or Telegram in the alert nodes, or OpenAI for another chat model.

Additional info
Tokens, passwords, API keys, bearer headers and email addresses are masked before anything is stored, emailed or sent to the AI. Once OpenAI has triaged an error, the verdict is reused for every repeat. There is deliberately no endpoint to register apps or change tokens: edit the table, so nobody can rewrite a token from outside. Emails are in Italian; their texts live in the Code nodes named on the canvas.

workflows.name: Monitor Unraid server health and send alerts with Telegram
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors an Unraid server via its GraphQL API, scanning new syslog warnings every minute and running broader health checks every five minutes, then sends deduplicated alerts with suggested next steps to a Telegram chat, with optional Unraid notifications and container auto-restarts.

How it works
Runs on two schedules: every minute for syslog monitoring and every five minutes for health checks.
Calls the Unraid GraphQL API to fetch either only the newly appended syslog lines or a full health snapshot (array, disks, SMART, Docker, notifications, CPU/memory).
Classifies syslog lines and health findings by severity and generates actionable alert details and suggested next steps.
Normalizes alerts and throttles repeats using stored state so the same issue is only sent once per configured time window.
Optionally sends the alert text to a connected chat model for short triage guidance and appends it to the alert.
Sends the formatted alert to Telegram, and optionally mirrors it into Unraid’s notification system and auto-starts stopped autostart Docker containers before reporting the result back to Telegram.

Setup
Create an Unraid admin API key (Unraid Settings → Management Access → API Keys) and configure an HTTP Header Auth credential that sends it as header name x-api-key.
Add a Telegram bot credential and set the target chat ID in cfg.telegramChatId.
Update cfg.unraidUrl to your Unraid WebGUI base URL (HTTPS) and adjust alert options like cfg.minSeverity and cfg.throttleMinutes.
(Optional) Enable cfg.alsoUnraidNotification to create Unraid notifications and/or cfg.autoRestartContainers to auto-start stopped autostart containers.
(Optional) Connect a chat model to the AI triage step and enable it if you want AI-generated guidance included in alerts.

workflows.name: Monitor SSL certificates and security headers with Apify, Slack, and Gmail alerts
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors SSL certificate expiry and security headers for a list of websites using Apify, stores the last known state in an n8n Data Table, and sends change-based alerts and a weekly summary to Slack, Gmail, and an optional webhook.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule, on demand, or on Mondays for the weekly summary, and loads the site list and notification settings from the CONFIG block.
Creates (if needed) and reads the ssl_monitor_state n8n Data Table to keep track of each site’s last known grade, certificate status, and open issues.
On daily/manual runs, calls the Apify “Security Headers & SSL Audit” Actor to audit each site’s HTTPS/certificate status, redirects, and security headers.
Compares the latest audit results with the stored state to detect new, changed, reminder-due, and resolved issues, with “site unreachable” only alerting after consecutive failed checks.
Saves the updated per-site state back to the ssl_monitor_state Data Table and builds a single consolidated alert message when any changes are detected.
Routes alerts by severity and sends them to the enabled channels via Slack, Gmail, and/or an HTTP webhook, retrying sends without blocking other channels.
On weekly summary runs, generates a summary from the stored state (without running Apify) and sends it through the same notification channels.

Setup
Create an Apify account and add an HTTP Header Auth credential with Authorization: Bearer  for the Apify request.
Add Slack credentials and set the target channel in CONFIG if you want Slack notifications.
Add Gmail credentials and set the recipient address and minimum severity in CONFIG if you want email notifications.
If using a webhook (for example Discord or Microsoft Teams), enable it in CONFIG and paste the webhook URL.
Update CONFIG with your site domains, certificate warning/critical thresholds, minimum headers grade, and reminder/consecutive-failure settings before activating the workflow.

Requirements
n8n with Data Tables (tested on 2.43), an Apify account (
Security Headers & SSL Audit Actor) and Slack and/or Gmail.

Customization
criticalReminderDays, email.minSeverity and confirmUnreachableChecks. Set previewWeeklySummary to true to test the summary. About $0.003 per site per check on Apify.

Additional info
Disclosure: the Apify Actor used here was built and is published by the author of this template (EdenWorks). You pay Apify's usage price when it runs and the author earns part of that fee. Apify's free plan credits cover light use.

workflows.name: Monitor FortiGate WAN health and clear top bandwidth users via Gmail
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Monitors FortiGate SD-WAN link health and real-time bandwidth usage. Sends Gmail reports and alerts for WAN outages, congestion, and slow connections. Supports secure, passphrase-verified email commands to identify the top bandwidth user and optionally clear their sessions through SSH, enabling automated network visibility, troubleshooting, and traffic management.

How it works
Triggers either when a matching Gmail message is received or every 10 minutes on a schedule.
Parses the newest allowed email command to decide whether to run a read-only report or request a session clear, and loads the full email to verify the sender for kill requests.
Queries the FortiGate REST API for SD-WAN members, health-check status, interface bandwidth capacity, and FortiView top sources and destinations.
Analyzes WANs as OK/SLOW/CHOKED/DOWN based on capacity, latency, and packet loss thresholds, and selects an eligible top private-IP bandwidth user that is not in the protected list.
If a verified email command requests it, connects to the FortiGate via SSH to clear sessions for the selected top source, waits 10 seconds, and re-queries top sources and SD-WAN members.
Builds an HTML email report and sends it via Gmail for every email command, or only on WAN problems and once on recovery for scheduled monitoring.

Setup
Create a FortiGate REST API admin and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential with an Authorization Bearer token for the FortiGate API requests.
Create a FortiGate CLI admin with SSH access from your n8n host and configure an SSH credential for the session-clearing step.
Connect a Gmail account for reading command emails and sending reports, then update the Gmail search query to include your chosen passphrase.
In the workflow settings values, set your FortiGate URL, allowed sender emails, report recipient, WAN interface names, protected IPs, and any thresholds (choke/latency/loss, cooldown, top N).

workflows.name: Review and monitor KYB ownership chains with GLEIF, OpenAI and Gmail
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow accepts KYB ownership-review requests via webhook, pulls corporate ownership-chain data from the GLEIF API, generates a structured risk memo with OpenAI, and manages human approvals and notifications through Gmail, while logging outcomes in n8n Data Tables and re-checking accepted clients weekly for changes.

How it works
Receives a header-authenticated webhook request containing an LEI (or legal name and country) and validates the input, including ISO 17442 check digits for LEIs.
Looks up the entity in the GLEIF API, ensures the match is unambiguous, and checks n8n Data Tables for an earlier open review or a recent accepted decision. This lookup can reuse a known case, but simultaneous requests are not serialized.
Walks the GLEIF direct-parent chain up to a configured maximum depth, captures reporting exceptions, and also fetches the ultimate-parent relationship to complete the chain context.
Applies rule-based KYB flags (for example FATF-listed country links, lapsed/withheld registry data, circular ownership, or declaration discrepancies) and calculates a minimum risk-rating floor plus a suggested document list.
Uses an OpenAI agent (with optional GLEIF lookups and prior-review retrieval) to produce a structured memo and then emails a review pack to the reviewer via Gmail with a decision form link.
Routes the reviewer’s decision to accept, request documents, escalate, or ask up to two follow-up questions to the OpenAI agent, and requires a second approver via Gmail for accepting high-risk cases.
Writes the final decision to the kyb_reviews table, optionally upserts a monitoring baseline in kyb_monitoring for accepted cases, and notifies the requester and (if escalated) the compliance officer by email.
Runs every Monday on a schedule to re-check monitored clients in GLEIF and, when the ownership fingerprint changes, attempts to reopen a review by posting back into the same webhook. A successful intake acknowledgement is not a completed review.

Setup
Run the manual setup trigger once to create the kyb_reviews and kyb_monitoring n8n Data Tables (or confirm they already exist).
Create credentials for Gmail, an OpenAI API key (Chat model), and an HTTP Header Auth credential for the intake webhook and for the “reopen review” HTTP request.
Replace the placeholder reviewer, senior approver, compliance officer, and ops alert email addresses in the workflow settings nodes.
Copy the production webhook URL for the intake endpoint into the monitoring configuration so the weekly checker can reopen reviews through the webhook.
(Recommended) Set this workflow as its own error workflow so failures trigger the Gmail ops alert message.

Requirements
An n8n version with Data Tables and compatible Gmail approval nodes, cloud or self-hosted. Check node compatibility in your instance before activation
An OpenAI API key (gpt-4.1-mini by default). Usage varies with tool iterations and reviewer follow-up questions
A Gmail account for the review pack, the senior approval and the notifications; no key needed for GLEIF (free public API)

Customization
Edit severities, suggested documents, legal-form patterns and the rating thresholds in "Assess ownership risk flags", and REUSE_DAYS / OPEN_REVIEW_DAYS in "Check open reviews and reuse window".
Update fatf_black_list, fatf_grey_list and fatf_list_date after each FATF plenary, and add your own list in extra_high_risk_countries (for example the EU list of high-risk third countries).
Change MAX_FOLLOW_UPS and the senior approval rule in "Apply review policy", and the waiting times in the Wait and Gmail approval nodes.
Change the weekly schedule, or send the alerts to Slack or Microsoft Teams instead of Gmail.
Replace the OpenAI model with Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral or a local model through Ollama.

Additional info
Limitations: GLEIF Level 2 data shows accounting-consolidation parents, not beneficial owners; the workflow never names a natural person as beneficial owner and asks for a UBO declaration instead. Only entities with an LEI are covered (others get HTTP 422 and need a manual check). Parent data is self-reported and can be lapsed or uncorroborated; it is flagged but not corrected. No sanctions, PEP or adverse media screening is included. The FATF lists in the settings are dated 30 October 2026 and must be kept up to date. Client names, GLEIF data and declared owners are sent to your AI provider. This is decision support for trained compliance staff, not legal advice; a person always makes the decision.
Operation and recovery
Review and senior-approval links are sensitive bearer links; form-entered reviewer details are not independent identity verification. Set mailbox access and retention for your deployment.

The current monitoring branches save the check result and attempt the reopen request in parallel. If that request fails or its response is uncertain, inspect the original execution, the case audit for the LEI and the monitoring row before retrying. A request may have succeeded before its response was lost. Reconcile an existing case; resend the original authenticated change-alert payload only when no corresponding case exists and the failure is confirmed. Do not clear the accepted ownership baseline or assume the weekly job will retry the same saved fingerprint automatically.

workflows.name: Monitor urgent App Store reviews with Apify, OpenAI, Google Sheets and Slack
workflows.description:
Pulls the newest Apple App Store reviews for the app IDs you list, keeps only reviews it has not seen before, and scores each one for urgency from the star rating, complaint keywords (crash, refund, cancel...), helpful votes and recency. Built for product, support and community teams who want bad reviews in front of a person the same day, and for agencies tracking client apps.

How it works
Daily schedule / manual run reads every setting from Config. A weekly schedule uses the same Config to send a report instead of running the actor.
Starts the Apify actor asynchronously, then waits and polls the run; FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT or too many polls stop with an error.
Downloads the dataset, validates rows and dedupes within the run and across runs (workflow static data, dedupeMemoryDays).
A transparent rule score runs first, then an LLM chain with a structured output parser reads each record against your plain-English aiCriteria and returns a fit score, verdict, summary, outreach angle and red flags. Calls are batched with a delay for rate limits, retried, and fall back to the rule score if the model fails.
Upserts every row to Google Sheets. Hot rows go to Slack as one approve / dismiss message (send-and-wait, 24 h limit) and the decision is written back to the sheet; warm rows go to an HTML email digest; cold rows stay in the sheet.
Weekly report: reads the sheet, summarises the last 7 days (tiers, approvals, top 10) and emails it.
A separate Error Trigger branch posts any failure to Slack.

Setup (about 15 minutes)
Create an HTTP Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value Bearer  (Apify Console > Settings > API & Integrations). Select it on the 3 Apify HTTP nodes.
Create a Google Sheet with a tab named in sheetTab and a header row matching the sheet columns (see Upsert to Google Sheets, plus status and reviewedAt). Paste its ID into googleSheetId.
Connect OpenAI (or swap the chat model sub-node for Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama...), Slack and Gmail; set slackChannelId and digestEmail in Config (also the channel on Slack: error alert).
In Config set actorInput.appIds (the number in an App Store URL, e.g. id324684580), actorInput.countries, complaintKeywords, hotScore and warmScore. Use actorInput.sinceDate to limit how far back each run looks.
Write your ideal-lead description in aiCriteria; set aiWeight (0 = rules only, 1 = AI only).
Run once manually, check the sheet, then activate.

Customize
Edit weights in Score review urgency (1 star 45, keywords up to 30, recency 15, helpful votes 15, detail 5).
Raise maxReviewsPerApp for busy apps, or set deltaMode and a stateKey in actorInput to have the actor itself return only new reviews.
The AI node drafts a reply angle for each hot review; nothing is posted back to the App Store.
Swap Gmail/Slack for Teams, Discord, HubSpot, Airtable, etc. Each delivery node only reads $json.

Disclosure: I maintain these Apify actors (account transparent_meteorite). The actor is a paid pay-per-event Apify tool; check its Store page for current pricing before scheduling.

workflows.name: Monitor web product prices and send change alerts with HTTP and Telegram
workflows.description:
Quick Overview
This workflow runs hourly to scrape product prices from web pages using HTTP requests and CSS selectors, compares them to previously stored values, and sends Telegram alerts when prices change or drop.

How it works
Runs every hour on a schedule trigger.
Loads your product list (name, URL, and CSS selector), plus alert preferences like chat ID and whether to alert only on drops.
Downloads each product page via HTTP and extracts the price text from the HTML using the provided CSS selector.
Parses the extracted price into a number, compares it with the last stored price in workflow static data, and keeps only real changes (optionally only decreases).
Sends a formatted Telegram message with the old price, new price, percentage change, and a link to the product page.

Setup
Create a Telegram bot and add Telegram API credentials in n8n.
Update the Telegram chat ID, the onlyDrops setting, and the products list (URL and CSS selector) in the alert settings.
Execute the workflow once manually to initialize stored prices, then activate it to run on the hourly schedule.

workflows.description:
Runs your Amazon keyword searches through Apify, treats a changed price as a new event (the dedupe key includes the price), and scores each product on discount versus list price, rating, review volume, monthly purchase volume, badges and your price ceiling. Built for resellers, deal watchers and brand teams tracking a category.

How it works
Daily schedule / manual run reads every setting from Config. A weekly schedule uses the same Config to send a report instead of running the actor.
Starts the Apify actor asynchronously, then waits and polls the run; FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT or too many polls stop with an error.
Downloads the dataset, validates rows and dedupes within the run and across runs (workflow static data, dedupeMemoryDays).
A transparent rule score runs first, then an LLM chain with a structured output parser reads each record against your plain-English aiCriteria and returns a fit score, verdict, summary, outreach angle and red flags. Calls are batched with a delay for rate limits, retried, and fall back to the rule score if the model fails.
Upserts every row to Google Sheets. Hot rows go to Slack as one approve / dismiss message (send-and-wait, 24 h limit) and the decision is written back to the sheet; warm rows go to an HTML email digest; cold rows stay in the sheet.
Weekly report: reads the sheet, summarises the last 7 days (tiers, approvals, top 10) and emails it.
A separate Error Trigger branch posts any failure to Slack.

Setup (about 15 minutes)
Create an HTTP Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value Bearer  (Apify Console > Settings > API & Integrations). Select it on the 3 Apify HTTP nodes.
Create a Google Sheet with a tab named in sheetTab and a header row matching the sheet columns (see Upsert to Google Sheets, plus status and reviewedAt). Paste its ID into googleSheetId.
Connect OpenAI (or swap the chat model sub-node for Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama...), Slack and Gmail; set slackChannelId and digestEmail in Config (also the channel on Slack: error alert).
In Config set actorInput.keywords, countryCode, maxPrice, minRating, minReviews and watchBrands. Leave scrapeProductDetails off to keep runs cheap; turn it on for seller and category fields.
Write your ideal-lead description in aiCriteria; set aiWeight (0 = rules only, 1 = AI only).
Run once manually, check the sheet, then activate.

Customize
Edit weights in Score product deals (discount 30, rating 15, reviews 15, volume 15, badges 10, price 10, brand 10).
Add minPrice, maxPrice, primeOnly or department to actorInput to filter at the source.
Swap Gmail/Slack for Teams, Discord, HubSpot, Airtable, etc. Each delivery node only reads $json.

Disclosure: I maintain these Apify actors (account transparent_meteorite). The actor is a paid pay-per-event Apify tool; check its Store page for current pricing before scheduling.

workflows.name: Monitor AI crawler policy signals via HTTP, Data Tables, email and Slack

user.name: Ad Astra Connect
user.bio: Tested, documented n8n workflows for operations, monitoring and small-business automation. Every template is imported and run end to end on a clean instance before release. Ad Astra Connect, Toronto.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Track published AI crawler rules on selected websites and optionally monitor llms.txt presence and content hashes. Receive one email for baselines or changes, with persistent snapshots in a Data Table.

How it works
A manual trigger or hourly tick gated by policyCheckHour in Config loads per-site snapshots once daily from a Data Table.
Fetch public files using a descriptive User-Agent, a 20-second timeout, paced requests and up to three transient attempts. Preserve successful responses during retries.
Parse case-insensitive user-agent groups, select the most specific match, merge equally specific groups and fall back to *. Strip comments, handle BOM and CRLF, ignore empty restrictions, and use the longest matching root rule with Allow winning ties.
Compare each bot's status and canonical path lists, plus optional llms.txt presence and hash. A robots.txt 404 means allow all. Other fetch errors are reported without changing that site's saved snapshot.
Send one SMTP email if required, then upsert successful snapshots by siteKey. No change sends no email. New baselines can be silent through Config.

Setup
Create a Data Table with siteKey, robotsHash, policyJson and llmsTxt as String columns and checkedAt as Date. Enter its ID, site origins, bot tokens and email addresses in Config, then select an SMTP credential. Run twice manually before publishing the daily schedule. See SETUP.md for details.
Requires n8n 2.8.4, Data Tables, an SMTP credential and outbound public HTTP access.

Requirements
n8n 2.8.4, Data Tables, an SMTP credential and outbound public HTTP access. Public GET requests require no API credentials. Keep workflow executions sequential. The included test harness requires Node 20 and cached n8n 2.8.4.

Customization
Edit Config for origins, crawler tokens, llms.txt checks, baseline emails, request pacing, addresses and policyCheckHour (0 to 23, default 9). The fixed hourly trigger checks the selected hour in the workflow or instance timezone; manual checks run immediately. A fuller version could also audit meta robots tags and X-Robots-Tag headers across many pages.

Additional info
Who is this for
Website owners, marketing teams and IT teams tracking published AI crawler preferences on a small list of public websites.

What it does
Fetches robots.txt and evaluates configured crawler tokens as blocked, allowed or partial, with their allow and disallow paths. Optionally checks llms.txt presence and SHA-256 hash without storing its content. Sends one escaped HTML summary for new baselines or meaningful changes, including short added and removed robots.txt lines. robots.txt is a voluntary convention; this template reports what sites publish and does not assess legal compliance.

Tested: parent-run mock and live suites passed on 2026-10-23 with n8n 2.8.4, including real import, Data Tables, SMTP rejection recovery, unchanged-run silence and three public sites. The review subsequently added a Config schedule gate and disabled duplicate native HTTP retries; its offline checks pass, but the final export needs a parent end-to-end rerun. See TESTING.md.

Third-party product names are used only to describe compatibility. This template is not affiliated with or endorsed by those companies.

A daily schedule reads your Watchlist and History tabs, drops duplicate or inactive rows and skips URLs checked in the last few hours.

In the Config node set sheetId and slackChannelId; optionally adjust minChangePct, minConfidence, minHoursBetweenChecks and runSummary.
Add Google Sheets, Slack and Google Gemini credentials.
Execute once to record a baseline, then activate.
Save the workflow and verify the Config node holds your own sheetId and slackChannelId before activating the trigger.

workflows.name: Monitor niche YouTube breakouts with DeepSeek and Telegram digests

user.name: Shuo Yuan
user.bio: I build n8n workflows and data pipelines for the repetitive parts of research and operations: web data collection, cleaning, LLM classification, and human-approval steps before anything is written to your systems. I have also built a retrieval system over regulatory documents where every answer stays tied to its source and version. I work in English and Chinese. Notes on how I build: iuschro.com

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to pull YouTube trending videos and keyword-based search results via the YouTube Data API, deduplicates them in an n8n Data Table, scores breakout potential with DeepSeek, and sends threshold-based breakout alerts and a ranked digest to Telegram.

How it works
Runs every day at 08:00 on a schedule.
Fetches the current YouTube “most popular” chart for the configured region and searches YouTube for videos matching your niche keywords from the last 24 hours, then hydrates those search results with video statistics.
Merges and deduplicates both result sets by video ID and calculates momentum metrics like views per hour, engagement rate, and a deterministic base score.
Skips any video already recorded in an n8n Data Table, then upserts newly found videos into the Data Table as “seen” for future deduplication.
Sends the new videos to DeepSeek to generate an LLM breakout score and reason (falling back to the deterministic score if the DeepSeek request fails) and calculates a blended final score.
Sends an immediate Telegram message for videos at or above the alert threshold, and aggregates mid-range videos into a ranked daily Telegram digest while ignoring anything below the digest threshold.

Setup
Create a Google Cloud API key with YouTube Data API v3 enabled and add it to n8n as an HTTP Query Auth credential (parameter name key) used by the YouTube HTTP Request nodes.
Create a DeepSeek API key and add it to n8n as an HTTP Header Auth credential (for example, Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DEEPSEEK_KEY).
Create a Telegram bot, add Telegram credentials in n8n, and replace YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID in both Telegram send steps.
Create an n8n Data Table with columns for video_id, title, channel, url, source, first_views, and first_seen, then replace YOUR_DATA_TABLE_ID in both Data Table steps.
Update the monitoring values (region code, niche keywords, digest size, and score thresholds) in the workflow’s configuration step before activating.

Runs every hour on a schedule.

Update the feed/site URLs, optional include/exclude keyword arrays, and the stateName value so each monitor has its own memory.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth credentials, paste your spreadsheet URL/ID into the Google Sheets node, and create a sheet tab named Feed log.

workflows.name: Monitor PR TIMES competitor press releases with OpenAI and Microsoft Teams

user.name: Yuji
user.bio:
Marketing lead at a Japanese software company. I build practical n8n workflows for Japanese businesses, using AI to handle the Japanese language and business customs in everyday work.
日本の業務でそのまま使える、AIを組み込んだ n8n ワークフローを公開しています。

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every weekday morning, reads PR TIMES RSS feeds for a list of competitor company IDs, uses OpenAI to score relevance and generate short summaries, and posts a single Adaptive Card with the relevant updates to a Microsoft Teams channel via an incoming webhook.

How it works
Runs every weekday morning on a schedule.
Loads a configured list of competitors (PR TIMES company_id values), a watch topic, a product description, an output language, and a lookback window.
Fetches each competitor’s PR TIMES RSS feed and keeps only releases published within the configured number of past days.
Skips releases that have already been processed in previous workflow executions using the release link as the deduplication key.
Sends each new release’s title and opening text to OpenAI to assign a relevance level (high/medium/low), a category, a short summary, and a “why it matters” line.
Keeps only high- and medium-relevance releases, aggregates them into a single list, and posts them to Microsoft Teams as one Adaptive Card message via a webhook.

Setup
Update the competitor list (name and PR TIMES company_id), topic, product description, output language, and days_back value in the Prepare Competitor Settings node.
Add an OpenAI API credential and select it in the OpenAI GPT-5 Mini node.
Create a Microsoft Teams Workflows incoming webhook (for example, "Send webhook alerts to a chat") and paste the webhook URL into the Post to Microsoft Teams node.

Requirements
An OpenAI API key (or another chat model supported by the Basic LLM Chain)
Microsoft Teams with the Workflows app
Competitors that publish press releases on PR TIMES

Customization
Change the schedule or the number of days to look back.
Edit the relevance rules in the Analyze and Summarize Release node to fit your market.
Replace the Teams node with Slack, email, or another channel.

Additional info
PR TIMES is a Japanese press release distribution service. Releases are usually written in Japanese, and the workflow can summarize them in English or any other language you set. Only the title and the opening text from the RSS feed are used, so the AI is told not to add facts that are not there.

workflows.name: Monitor JSON business health checks and send Slack alerts

user.name: Ahmad Yar
user.bio: I’m Ahmad. For the last three years, I’ve worked across marketing, CRM and revenue operations, close to the actual work of generating demand, managing leads and keeping businesses moving.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs hourly to check an HTTPS JSON endpoint for expected HTTP status and business-rule assertions, deduplicates repeated failures using n8n static data, and posts failure or recovery alerts to a Slack channel.

How it works
Runs every hour (or on manual execution) and loads the monitor configuration, including the target URL, expected status code, Slack channel ID, and up to four JSON field checks.
Validates the configuration and converts the check rows into structured assertions.
Sends an HTTP GET request to the target HTTPS endpoint and captures the full JSON response and status code.
Evaluates the response against the expected HTTP status and the configured business checks (equals, nonEmpty, minItems, or freshWithinMinutes) and produces a healthy/unhealthy result with issue codes.
Compares the current result to the previous run stored in n8n static workflow data to detect new failures, changed failures, reminder-worthy ongoing failures, or recoveries.
Posts a formatted alert message to Slack only when an alert is needed, otherwise it completes silently.

Setup
In the “EDIT HERE — URL, Checks & Alerts” node, set your HTTPS JSON GET endpoint, expected HTTP status, Slack channel ID, reminder interval, and at least one JSON path check with a supported rule.
Configure authentication in the HTTP Request node if your endpoint requires it (for example, Header Auth with an Authorization bearer token or X-API-Key).
Add a Slack credential with permission to post messages (chat:write), invite the bot to the target channel, and keep the workflow’s Slack channel selection bound to the configured channel ID.

workflows.name: Monitor hotel competitor rates on Booking.com and tiket.com with MrScraper, Gemini and Telegram
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to scrape competitor hotel rates from Booking.com and tiket.com using MrScraper, stores rate history in Google Sheets, generates an Indonesian summary with Google Gemini, and sends a combined watchlist and area market scan report to Telegram.

How it works
Runs every day at 15:00 (Asia/Jakarta) and starts both the competitor watchlist scan and a Booking.com area search scan.
Reads competitor listings from Google Sheets and builds dated detail-page URLs for the next two weekends, routing Booking.com to structured scraping and tiket.com to rendered-page scraping.
Uses MrScraper to extract room types and prices from Booking.com, and uses MrScraper plus Google Gemini to extract room types and prices from tiket.com markdown.
Normalizes rates, compares them to the existing Google Sheets history to detect confirmed price-level changes, then appends all observations to the Rate_History sheet and upserts the latest values into Current_Status.
Builds a report that includes platform health, market cheapest prices per listing and date, sold-out detection, cross-platform comparisons, date-to-date comparisons, and multi-day price trends.
Scrapes the top listings from a Booking.com search results page for the configured city, extracts each listing’s cheapest rate, and appends the results to the Area_Scan sheet.
Uses Google Gemini to write a Telegram-friendly report (or falls back to a deterministic summary if Gemini fails) and sends a single combined message to a Telegram chat.

Setup
Install the community node package n8n-nodes-mrscraper (self-hosted n8n) and add MrScraper API credentials.
Create a Google Sheets OAuth credential, make a spreadsheet with the required tabs (Listings, Rate_History, Current_Status, Area_Scan), and replace YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_ID in all Google Sheets nodes.
Populate the Listings sheet with competitor properties, including platform (booking.com or tiket.com) and the property detail URLs.
Add Google Gemini credentials for the Gemini nodes and ensure your API quota supports the daily extraction and report generation.
Create a Telegram bot and credential, then set YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID in the Telegram node to the target user or group chat.
Optionally customize the monitored stay dates and city by editing WEEKEND_COUNT in the request builder and AREA_CITY/DAY_OFFSET in the area scan URL builder.

Requirements
Self-hosted n8n with the community node n8n-nodes-mrscraper
MrScraper account and API token. The Free plan allows 10 parallel requests
Google Sheets OAuth2 credential and a copy of the sheet template
Gemini API key. 1 run uses up to 3 Gemini requests
Telegram bot token from @BotFather and your chat ID

Customization
Platforms and stay dates: EXTRACTION_PATH and WEEKEND_COUNT in Build Requests
Alert threshold: ALERT_THRESHOLD_PCT in Normalize Booking Rates and Normalize Markdown Rates
Area scan city and check-in offset: AREA_CITY and DAY_OFFSET in Build Area Scan URL
Report language: the report is in Indonesian. Edit the prompt in Gemini Write Report and the labels in Compose Telegram Message

Additional info
Sheet template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1toPSjbY7JspOkHNheB7D3L-ezYAvjM7rBaFr8oHOdlI/copy
1 run checks 4 stay dates (the next 2 weekends) per listing. 10 listings = 40 page requests, plus 6 for the area scan.
MrScraper nodes use On Error: Continue. A failed page is saved with its status, and the run continues.

workflows.name: Monitor new Uniswap Base pools with GeckoTerminal and an HTML dashboard

user.name: Harry
user.bio: Automation engineer building production workflows for cross-border e-commerce and on-chain data. Every template I publish ends with a real side effect - a reply sent, a ticket logged, an alert raised - not just a JSON response.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors newly created Uniswap V3 pools on Base using the GeckoTerminal API, stores pool metrics and a simple risk score in an n8n Data Table, and serves an auto-refreshing HTML dashboard via a webhook.

How it works
Runs manually to fetch the latest Base new-pools feed from the GeckoTerminal API.
Parses each pool’s name and metrics (liquidity, 24h volume, and 24h transaction count), computes a risk score and risk level, and filters out major-token pairs and pools below the liquidity threshold.
Stores the resulting pool records in an n8n Data Table for later display.
Receives a webhook request for the dashboard page.
Loads all stored pool records from the n8n Data Table, deduplicates and sorts them by creation time, and calculates summary stats (total, last-hour count, and risk distribution).
Returns an HTML dashboard (auto-refreshing every 30 seconds) that shows the latest pool cards and links each pool to its GeckoTerminal page.

Setup
Create an n8n Data Table (for example, "new_pools_official") with the columns used by the workflow (pool address, token symbols/addresses, fee tier, liquidity, 24h volume, tx count, created_at, risk fields, and network).
In the Data Table nodes, select your Data Table for both storing new pools and retrieving all pools.
Publish the workflow and open the webhook URL at /webhook/new-pools-dashboard (prepend your n8n domain) to view the live dashboard.

workflows.name: Monitor AI citation changes for your domain with TriRank and SMTP email

user.name: TriRank
user.bio: We build TriRank, an AI search visibility platform for website owners and SEO teams. Our n8n templates turn cached AI citation readings into Slack and email alerts or downloadable CSV reports. Start with a free website audit at trirankai.com.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Read a domain’s cached AI citation measurements from TriRank each Monday and email a baseline or changed reading. The workflow watches existing measurements; it does not run new AI checks. Missing or stale measurements are reported separately from measured zero citations.

How it works
Run every Monday at 09:00 in the n8n workflow timezone.
Sets the domain to monitor (and whether to notify on the first run).
Read cached measurements from https://trirankai.com/api/signals/. This is a read-only request; it does not trigger new AI probes. HTTP errors and rate limits are reported as unavailable data.
Compare the stored reading with this run using n8n workflow static data. Report measured citations, measured zero citations, partial coverage or no fresh measurement as distinct states. Unchanged readings produce no email; the first run can send a baseline.
Checks whether a message was produced and, if so, sends it as a plain-text email via SMTP.

Setup
Run the free audit for your domain at https://trirankai.com/audit to seed its measurement. Complete the human verification yourself. Old citation data can expire and needs a fresh audit; this workflow does not refresh it.
Set your domain in Configure domain and choose notifyOnFirstRun. Activate the workflow after SMTP setup, and check its timezone. Static data persists during active scheduled runs, not manual test executions.
Add an SMTP credential, then set the From and To addresses in the email step.
(Optional) Create a TriRank API key and configure it as an x-api-key header credential on the HTTP request to increase the daily read allowance.

Requirements
An n8n instance and an SMTP credential. No TriRank account is required for 60 anonymous reads per IP per day. Store optional x-api-key authentication in a Header Auth credential; never include credentials in the workflow JSON.

Customization
Change the schedule or disable the first-run baseline. Keep missing measurements separate from measured zero citations. Quiet weeks send no email.

Additional info
TriRank: https://trirankai.com
Free audit and measurement setup: https://trirankai.com/audit
This email version is intended for users without a Slack workspace. It sends existing cached results, not fresh AI-check results.
